settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: Expression is parsed once in the constructor from configuration, not from the incoming request
createELContext() binds a narrow ELRequestMatcherContext root object limited to hasIpAddress/hasHeader
matches() only evaluates the pre-parsed expression against request attributes
candidates.description: ELRequestMatcher parses a SpEL expression string in its constructor and evaluates it inside matches(HttpServletRequest) via createELContext() which returns an ELRequestMatcherContext root object exposing hasIpAddress(String) and hasHeader(String). The expression text comes from the constructor argument (developer configuration), so request data only influences arguments passed into the context methods, not the parsed expression itself. No call site passing request-derived strings into the constructor was observed in the read span. Recorded as an inspection note, not a confirmed vulnerability.
missing_evidence: No call site feeding request-derived data into the ELRequestMatcher constructor was read
No configuration file in the read spans shows an attacker-controllable expression
preconditions: Application constructs ELRequestMatcher with an expression string derived from untrusted input (not observed)
candidates.title: SpEL expression evaluation in ELRequestMatcher uses a default SpEL context (expression source is configuration, not request)

counter_evidence: Expression originates from the @AuthenticationPrincipal annotation and is evaluated per request but authored statically
Expression root object is limited to the authenticated principal
setBeanResolver is populated from constructor-injected configuration, not from request input
candidates.description: resolvePrincipal reads an expression attribute from the @AuthenticationPrincipal annotation, parses it with SpelExpressionParser, and evaluates it on a StandardEvaluationContext whose root object is the authenticated principal (with a bean resolver set from configuration). The expression text is authored in the annotation at compile time; per-request data reaches only the principal object that becomes the expression root. The general-purpose StandardEvaluationContext is used, but no untrusted expression source was identified in the read span. Recorded as an inspection note, not a confirmed vulnerability.
missing_evidence: No evidence that any annotation expression value is populated from external/request input
No call site or configuration source overriding the parser with untrusted strings was read
preconditions: An annotation expression would need to be attacker-controlled (annotations are developer-authored; not observed as untrusted)
candidates.title: SpEL expression evaluation in AuthenticationPrincipalArgumentResolver against a StandardEvaluationContext
